findings.highlight: I was breathing hard when I was running down the hill, but my fatigue went away by the time I got to the intersection.
findings.evidenceJa: 息が乱れて走りづらかったが、それも交差点まで降りた頃にはなくなっていた
findings.governingReading: His disordered breathing, which made running difficult, has subsided by the intersection.
findings.explanation: The English changes the thing that subsides from breathlessness to fatigue.

findings.highlight: for five kilometers
findings.evidenceJa: 実に五キロ近い道のり
findings.governingReading: The route is nearly five kilometers.
findings.explanation: The English turns an approximation into an exact distance.

findings.highlight: readying myself to have Kotomine talk
findings.evidenceJa: 力ずくでも聞き出してやる
findings.governingReading: Shirou steels himself to force the information out of Kotomine if necessary.
findings.explanation: The English omits the readiness to use force.

findings.highlight: I did not think you were admirable enough
findings.evidenceJa: 殊勝な男ではなかった筈だが
findings.governingReading: Kotomine says Shirou was never the commendably pious sort who would pray when cornered.
findings.explanation: The English turns context-specific piety into a judgment that Shirou lacks sufficient general admirability.

findings.highlight: you seem disturbed
findings.evidenceJa: 確かに余裕はなさそうだな
findings.governingReading: Kotomine observes that Shirou indeed appears to have no composure or margin to spare.
findings.explanation: The English replaces lack of leeway with generic emotional disturbance.

findings.highlight: Matou Zouken coordinated
findings.evidenceJa: 間桐臓硯によって調整された
findings.governingReading: Sakura was adjusted or prepared by Matou Zouken as a black Grail.
findings.explanation: The English uses “coordinated” without an object, obscuring Zouken’s physical and magical modification of her.

findings.highlight: I stop
findings.evidenceJa: 言葉に詰まる
findings.governingReading: Shirou is at a loss for words.
findings.explanation: The English changes a speech reaction into unspecified stopping.

findings.highlight: you don’t have a reason to
findings.evidenceJa: おまえにそんな理由はないだろう
findings.governingReading: Shirou says Kotomine has no such reason—that is, no motive comparable to Shirou’s wish to protect Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English weakens the pointed comparison into having no reason at all.

findings.highlight: you cannot kill what has not yet come into existence
findings.evidenceJa: 誕生しうるもの、生まれようとするモノを殺す事は出来ない
findings.governingReading: Kotomine says he cannot kill something capable of birth and actively trying to be born.
findings.explanation: The English reduces both capacity and striving to simple nonexistence.

findings.highlight: Andhe sacrificed his entire Magic Crest
findings.evidenceJa: こいつは自分の魔術刻印を全て使って桜を助けてくれた
findings.governingReading: The sentence should read “And he sacrificed his entire Magic Crest.”
findings.explanation: The English runs two words together.

findings.highlight: the contents of the Holy Grail appearing through Matou Sakura
findings.evidenceJa: 間桐桜から漏れた聖杯の中身
findings.governingReading: Zouken’s account identifies the shadow as Grail contents leaking from Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English replaces leakage with neutral appearance, weakening the model Kotomine is about to correct.

findings.highlight: something that’s leaked out of the gate
findings.evidenceJa: 桜という聖杯から漏れているモノ
findings.governingReading: Shirou asks why the thing leaking from the Holy Grail that is Sakura attacks indiscriminately.
findings.explanation: The English replaces Sakura-as-Grail with an unspecified gate.

findings.highlight: ruining Sakura
findings.evidenceJa: 桜を蝕んでいる
findings.governingReading: Shirou imagines the thing within the Grail eating away at or corroding Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English weakens the bodily invasive image to generic ruin.

findings.highlight: My vision wavers
findings.evidenceJa: 視界が軋む
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s field of vision seems to creak or grind under the recognition.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the harsh synesthetic strain with ordinary wavering vision.

findings.highlight: This is too ridiculous to be true
findings.evidenceJa: そんな馬鹿げたモノ、いる筈がないと否定して
findings.governingReading: Shirou actively rejects the possibility that such an absurd thing could exist.
findings.explanation: The English states implausibility but omits his act of denial.

findings.highlight: a swirl that interpreted everything as slaughter
findings.evidenceJa: あらゆる解釈をもって人間を殺す方向性を持った『渦』
findings.governingReading: The contaminated power became a vortex directed toward killing humans under every interpretation.
findings.explanation: The English makes the vortex itself interpret everything as slaughter and blurs the governing directionality.

findings.highlight: I still found the Holy Grail worthy
findings.evidenceJa: 私はそれでも変わらぬと聖杯を認め
findings.governingReading: Kotomine says that even so, he accepted or acknowledged the Grail without changing his position.
findings.explanation: The English invents a judgment of worthiness.

findings.highlight: the cause of it
findings.evidenceJa: 全ての元凶
findings.governingReading: Shirou saw the root cause of everything with his own eyes.
findings.explanation: The English weakens both total scope and root-cause force.

findings.highlight: The cup that receives the purest souls
findings.evidenceJa: 魂をくべる杯
findings.governingReading: The cup is one into which souls of the highest purity are fed like fuel.
findings.explanation: The English neutralizes the sacrificial or fuel-like action into reception.

findings.highlight: when a small amount of poison was mixed into it
findings.evidenceJa: 一粒の毒が混ざった程度で
findings.governingReading: A single grain or drop of poison was enough to discolor the whole.
findings.explanation: The English removes the pointed one-particle scale of the contamination.

findings.highlight: No matter how deep and magnificent the Holy Grail may have been
findings.evidenceJa: どれほど深遠で広大だろうと
findings.governingReading: No matter how profound and vast it was, the colorless Grail could not withstand the contaminant.
findings.explanation: The English changes spatial vastness into evaluative magnificence.

findings.highlight: a colored foreign substance
findings.evidenceJa: たった一人の、色のついた異分子
findings.governingReading: The overwhelming colorless expanse was defeated by one single colored foreign element, described with the counter for a person.
findings.explanation: The English omits both singular emphasis and the human counter, prematurely depersonalizing the contaminant.

findings.highlight: The fourth Holy Grail was too narrow
findings.evidenceJa: 四度目の聖杯は狭すぎた
findings.governingReading: The fourth Grail had insufficient capacity for full emergence.
findings.explanation: The English copies the spatial adjective literally and obscures the capacity claim.

findings.highlight: the phenomenon inside the Holy Grail
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯の中にいる現象
findings.governingReading: The script presents the entity as a “phenomenon” read as a “thing,” sustaining its uncertain ontological status.
findings.explanation: The English preserves only “phenomenon” and loses the thing/phenomenon double reading.

findings.highlight: expected baby
findings.evidenceJa: 出産予定児
findings.governingReading: Kotomine calls it an unborn child awaiting its scheduled birth.
findings.explanation: The English produces unnatural wording that can suggest a socially expected baby rather than a gestating entity due to be born.

findings.highlight: a legitimately made Holy Grail
findings.evidenceJa: 正しく作られた聖杯
findings.governingReading: Kotomine describes a Grail made correctly or according to proper construction.
findings.explanation: The English shifts technical construction into legitimacy.

findings.highlight: come into this world
findings.evidenceJa: 無から有に至るため
findings.governingReading: The transfer is the means by which the entity passes from nonbeing into being.
findings.explanation: The English gives only arrival in this world and omits the ontological transition.

findings.highlight: come into this world
findings.evidenceJa: この世に存在まれようとしている
findings.governingReading: The written “exist” is read as “be born,” joining existence and birth in one expression.
findings.explanation: The English omits the deliberate existence/birth double reading.

findings.highlight: permeating into the master
findings.evidenceJa: 寄り代への侵食
findings.governingReading: The curse invades its vessel or host, which is read here as “Master.”
findings.explanation: The English preserves only Master and loses the host-vessel basis of the relationship.

findings.highlight: once the power is completely succeeded
findings.evidenceJa: 力の継承が済んでしまえば
findings.governingReading: Once the succession or inheritance of power is complete, Sakura herself will transform into the shadow.
findings.explanation: The English uses an ungrammatical passive construction that obscures transfer completion.

findings.highlight: they would not be compatible
findings.evidenceJa: それと適合するだけの依り代ではない
findings.governingReading: An Einzbern Grail would not be a vessel compatible enough with the curse to produce Sakura’s outcome.
findings.explanation: The English loses the vessel and gives the plural pronoun “they” no clear antecedents.

findings.highlight: something that could give it shape
findings.evidenceJa: 自身を確かなカタチに“象どれる”依り代
findings.governingReading: The entity connected to a vessel capable of modeling it into a definite form.
findings.explanation: The English reduces the technical host or vessel to “something.”

findings.highlight: give it shape
findings.evidenceJa: 確かなカタチに“象どれる”依り代
findings.governingReading: The line plays written modeling or imaging against the reading “shape,” then contrasts definite and indefinite form.
findings.explanation: The English removes the written/read distinction and the image/form pattern.

findings.highlight: an expanding lump of flesh
findings.evidenceJa: ただ増殖するだけの肉の塊
findings.governingReading: The hypothetical result may be a lump of flesh that does nothing but proliferate.
findings.explanation: The English changes ongoing multiplication into physical expansion.

findings.highlight: Let me know the conclusion
findings.evidenceJa: 結論を知れ
findings.governingReading: Shirou orders himself to grasp the conclusion after inwardly demanding that Kotomine state it.
findings.explanation: The English turns the inward imperative into another request addressed to Kotomine.

findings.highlight: a human who was raised to be a Magic Circuit
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術回路として育てられた人間
findings.governingReading: Sakura is a human whose implanted material was cultivated as magical circuits.
findings.explanation: The English makes the human herself one singular Magic Circuit.

findings.highlight: ‘the sense of touch’ that leaked out
findings.evidenceJa: この世に漏れた“触覚”
findings.governingReading: The implanted object is the contaminant’s feeler or tactile appendage that leaked into this world during the prior war.
findings.explanation: The English literalizes 触覚 as the abstract sense of touch, making the implanted material incoherent.

findings.highlight: she still has command
findings.evidenceJa: 命令権は彼女にある
findings.governingReading: Sakura retains the formal authority to issue commands to the curse.
findings.explanation: The English weakens a defined right or authority into vague “command.”

findings.highlight: desire to kill people
findings.evidenceJa: 殺人嗜好
findings.governingReading: The curse’s “murderous predilection” is read as its directional orientation, joining appetite to programmed direction.
findings.explanation: The English reduces the layered expression to a generic desire to kill.

findings.highlight: The darkness in her will be given birth
findings.evidenceJa: 間桐桜が孕んだ闇は誕生する
findings.governingReading: The darkness Sakura carries will be born when either condition is met.
findings.explanation: The English is grammatically malformed.

findings.highlight: Sakura’s body will come out from beneath its darkness
findings.evidenceJa: 黒い影の下から、桜の体が現れる
findings.governingReading: Shirou imagines Sakura’s body appearing beneath the black shadow after its defeat.
findings.explanation: The English changes the concrete shadow into its abstract “darkness,” blurring that the shadow and Sakura are the same manifested body.

findings.highlight: I clutch my chest
findings.evidenceJa: 肉を抉るほど胸を押さえて
findings.governingReading: Shirou presses his chest hard enough to gouge into his flesh.
findings.explanation: The English omits the extreme force of the grip.

findings.highlight: force myself to breathe
findings.evidenceJa: 消えかけていた呼吸を再開させる
findings.governingReading: He restarts breathing that was on the verge of disappearing.
findings.explanation: The English omits that his breath was fading out and that he resumes it.

findings.highlight: Good and evil are what we decide on after it occurs
findings.evidenceJa: 善悪など、所詮発生した後に我々が決める事にすぎん
findings.governingReading: Kotomine argues that people assign good and evil only after a being has emerged.
findings.explanation: The English uses an unanchored “it occurs,” obscuring birth or emergence as the threshold in his argument.

findings.highlight: shadow has only been created from the host, Matou Sakura
findings.evidenceJa: 間桐桜という依り代から象った影
findings.governingReading: The shadow is a form modeled from the vessel that is Matou Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English generalizes the specific fashioning or modeling relation into creation.

findings.highlight: It shall receive punishment for its crime
findings.evidenceJa: 罪も罰も与えられるべきだろう
findings.governingReading: Kotomine says guilt and punishment should both be assigned after birth.
findings.explanation: The English presupposes an already established crime and omits the separate assignment of guilt.

findings.highlight: that which has not yet been born
findings.evidenceJa: 孵らざるもの
findings.governingReading: Kotomine calls it something that has not hatched.
findings.explanation: The English drops the hatching image that continues the gestation metaphor.

findings.highlight: cannot be punished
findings.evidenceJa: いまだ世に罪科を問われぬもの
findings.governingReading: It has not yet entered the world where it can be called to account for crimes.
findings.explanation: The English turns a temporal and jurisdictional claim into an inability to punish.

findings.highlight: A clear evil does not exist in this world
findings.evidenceJa: 明確な悪の定義など人の世には存在しない
findings.governingReading: Kotomine says no clear definition of evil exists in human society.
findings.explanation: The English says no clearly evil thing exists, changing an epistemic claim about definition into an ontological one.

findings.highlight: Would it not be the act of denying what is about to be born?
findings.evidenceJa: 絶対の悪ではないか
findings.governingReading: Kotomine proposes that stopping a being from birth may itself be absolute evil.
findings.explanation: The English omits “absolute evil,” the rhetorical conclusion of his argument.

findings.highlight: It’s not that I agree with Kotomine that Sakura should become the contents of the Holy Grail
findings.evidenceJa: そうなる事を否定しない、という言峰の言い分を許したワケじゃない
findings.governingReading: Shirou has not forgiven Kotomine’s refusal to reject Sakura’s transformation.
findings.explanation: The English changes toleration of a noninterventionist stance into agreement with a positive claim that Sakura should transform.

findings.highlight: too late to be a declaration of hostility
findings.evidenceJa: 宣戦布告にしては遅すぎる
findings.governingReading: The question comes too late to serve as a declaration of war.
findings.explanation: The English weakens explicit war language into generic hostility.

findings.highlight: the embryo
findings.evidenceJa: その胎児
findings.governingReading: Kotomine says he will defend the fetus Sakura carries.
findings.explanation: The English changes the developmental term to embryo.

findings.highlight: after Zouken or I remain
findings.evidenceJa: 俺たちと臓硯そのどちらかが残って
findings.governingReading: Kotomine wants to see what appears after either Shirou’s side or Zouken remains.
findings.explanation: The English narrows Shirou’s whole side to Shirou alone.

findings.highlight: He has no intention of forcing Sakura and altering her
findings.evidenceJa: 桜に無理強いさせて“変貌”させる気などない
findings.governingReading: Kotomine has no intention of coercing Sakura into transforming.
findings.explanation: The English coordinates forcing and altering as separate acts and blurs that transformation is what he will not force upon her.

findings.highlight: I will not say anything
findings.evidenceJa: 口出しはせん
findings.governingReading: Kotomine says he will not interfere or object if Shirou chooses to understand the treatment that way.
findings.explanation: The English reduces noninterference to literal silence.

findings.highlight: worrying about Sakura’s healthno, her mind
findings.evidenceJa: 桜の体いや、心を気遣って
findings.governingReading: Shirou corrects himself from Kotomine’s concern for Sakura’s body to concern for her mind.
findings.explanation: The English changes body to general health and runs the correction together.

findings.highlight: I still can’t tell for certain
findings.evidenceJa: 敵か味方か判らない
findings.governingReading: Shirou still cannot tell whether Kotomine is enemy or ally.
findings.explanation: The English omits the alternatives that define his uncertainty.

findings.highlight: he gives me advice
findings.evidenceJa: 敵である俺に助言をした
findings.governingReading: The priest gives advice to Shirou despite Shirou being his enemy.
findings.explanation: The English omits the adversarial relation that makes the help striking.

findings.highlight: if her mind can endure the power from the Holy Grail for a bit
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女の精神が少しでも耐えられるのなら
findings.governingReading: If Sakura’s mind can withstand even a little of the Grail’s power, the resulting sliver of time offers hope.
findings.explanation: The English turns the minimal degree of endurance into an imprecise duration before the duration is separately introduced.

findings.highlight: the baby within her and the crest worm
findings.evidenceJa: 刻印虫も、彼女の肉体を依り代にするモノも
findings.governingReading: Both the Crest Worms that make Sakura a Grail and the entity using her body as its vessel must be killed.
findings.explanation: The English imports Kotomine’s baby analogy as literal identity, singularizes the worm system, and omits the body-as-vessel relation.

findings.highlight: it could end up repeating the disaster that occurred ten years ago
findings.evidenceJa: しくじれば十年前の惨劇を繰り返す事になる
findings.governingReading: If the controller fails, the result will repeat the tragedy of ten years ago.
findings.explanation: The English turns a direct failure consequence into an impersonal possibility.

findings.highlight: I do have one hope
findings.evidenceJa: 少しはアテがある
findings.governingReading: Shirou has at least something or someone he can rely on for the plan.
findings.explanation: The English changes practical reliance into one abstract hope.

findings.highlight: It should be possible to tune with her sister’s mind and moderate the reaction from the Holy Grail
findings.evidenceJa: 同調し、聖杯からの反動を和らげる事も容易だろう
findings.governingReading: Kotomine expects Rin could readily synchronize with Sakura’s mind and soften the Grail’s recoil.
findings.explanation: The English weakens likely ease to bare possibility, copies “tune with” awkwardly, and reduces recoil to generic reaction.

findings.highlight: I’ll have to convince her to change our course of action once I get home
findings.evidenceJa: 帰ったらまずいの一番に、遠坂を説得して
findings.governingReading: Persuading Rin is the very first thing Shirou must do on returning.
findings.explanation: The English omits its absolute priority.

findings.highlight: I don’t approve of your opinion
findings.evidenceJa: アンタの言い分は認めない
findings.governingReading: Shirou refuses to accept Kotomine’s argument or position.
findings.explanation: The English recasts refusal to concede an argument as personal disapproval of an opinion.

findings.highlight: I stop
findings.evidenceJa: 去ろうとした足を止める
findings.governingReading: Shirou stops the feet that had already begun to carry him away.
findings.explanation: The English omits the interrupted departure.

findings.highlight: if I can return the favor
findings.evidenceJa: この借りが帳消しになるなら
findings.governingReading: Answering Kotomine’s question would cancel Shirou’s debt to him.
findings.explanation: The English turns cancellation of an unwanted debt into reciprocating a favor.

findings.highlight: the fact that she ate humans
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女が既に“人食い”である事
findings.governingReading: Kotomine labels Sakura already a “man-eater,” an identity that persists even if she ceases to be the Grail.
findings.explanation: The English turns the continuing identity into a completed past act.

findings.highlight: It is less painful that way
findings.evidenceJa: その方が楽であり
findings.governingReading: Kotomine calls death the easier course.
findings.explanation: The English specifies reduced pain, narrowing a broader claim about relief and burden.

findings.highlight: an apology to all who she has killed
findings.evidenceJa: 奪われた者たちへの謝罪
findings.governingReading: Kotomine frames Sakura’s death as an apology to those who were deprived, a phrase broad enough to include more than the dead themselves.
findings.explanation: The English narrows the injured party to people Sakura killed.

findings.highlight: she must repay the victims with something of equal value
findings.evidenceJa: 奪われた者は静まらない
findings.governingReading: The inward punitive logic says the deprived will not be appeased unless an equivalent is returned.
findings.explanation: The English states repayment but omits the victims’ continuing unrest as its rationale.

findings.highlight: My morals tell me
findings.evidenceJa: あらゆる常識が訴え続ける
findings.governingReading: Every conventional principle keeps insisting that Shirou kill Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English turns externalized, relentless common sense into Shirou’s own morals and omits persistence.

findings.highlight: if I truly pity the victims
findings.evidenceJa: 失われた者にすまないという気持ち
findings.governingReading: The pressure invokes feeling sorry toward those lost or a sense of owing them an apology.
findings.explanation: The English changes guilt and apology into pity.

findings.highlight: Many more lives will be lost
findings.evidenceJa: 何十倍もの命が失われる
findings.governingReading: Dozens of times as many lives will be lost if Sakura fully becomes the Grail.
findings.explanation: The English omits the stated magnitude.

findings.highlight: Innocent people
findings.evidenceJa: 無関係な人間
findings.governingReading: People with no involvement will die one-sidedly without understanding why.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes moral innocence for lack of involvement.

findings.highlight: I might bleed out of my eyes
findings.evidenceJa: 眼球から血液さえこぼれだしそう
findings.governingReading: It feels as though even blood might spill from Shirou’s eyeballs.
findings.explanation: “Bleed out” conventionally implies fatal exsanguination and overstates the image.

findings.highlight: Higher, wider, farther
findings.evidenceJa: より高く、より遠く、より広く
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu loved humanity on an ever higher, farther, and broader scale.
findings.explanation: The English leaves the comparative fragments unattached and reverses their order.

findings.highlight: he turned himself into the definite evil
findings.evidenceJa: 自身を絶対の悪とした
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu made himself the absolute evil for humanity’s sake.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes unnatural “definite evil” for absolute evil.

findings.highlight: trying to pick it back up after he threw it away
findings.evidenceJa: 切り捨てた後でさえ拾い上げた
findings.governingReading: Even after casting human feeling away, Kiritsugu picked it up again.
findings.explanation: The English weakens the completed recovery to an attempt.

findings.highlight: If I cannot obtain anything
findings.evidenceJa: 初めから持ち得ないのなら
findings.governingReading: Kotomine asks why he was born if he was constitutionally incapable of possessing the human feeling Kiritsugu had.
findings.explanation: The English broadens this specific deprivation into inability to obtain anything at all.

findings.highlight: you insist on having it both ways
findings.evidenceJa: おまえは両立する事しか実行できない
findings.governingReading: Kotomine says Shirou can act only by trying to make both sides coexist.
findings.explanation: The English adds insistence and the pejorative idiom “have it both ways.”

findings.highlight: It is posteriori
findings.evidenceJa: 後天的ではあるが
findings.governingReading: The defect is acquired rather than congenital, despite Kotomine’s paradoxical label that follows.
findings.explanation: The English uses malformed philosophical Latin instead of the medical or developmental contrast.

findings.highlight: You will not be able to save her after that
findings.evidenceJa: 間桐桜を取り戻す事もできなくなる
findings.governingReading: Once Zouken occupies the empty body, Sakura’s lost self can no longer be recovered.
findings.explanation: The English generalizes recovery of Sakura’s personhood into saving her.

findings.highlight: His main body is a parasite
findings.evidenceJa: 本体は人体に寄生する蟲
findings.governingReading: Zouken’s main body is an insect that parasitizes human bodies.
findings.explanation: The English omits both insect form and its specifically human host.

findings.highlight: the worm with his soul
findings.evidenceJa: 魂の容器にあたる脳虫
findings.governingReading: The brain worm serves as the vessel of Zouken’s soul.
findings.explanation: The English omits both “brain” and the vessel relation, making the soul sound merely contained in an ordinary worm.

findings.highlight: that tiny main body
findings.evidenceJa: 手のひらほどの本体
findings.governingReading: Zouken’s true body is about the size of a palm.
findings.explanation: The English replaces a concrete scale with vague smallness.

findings.highlight: If Rin is the positive, she is the negative
findings.evidenceJa: 凛が陽性だとしたらアレは陰性なのだろう
findings.governingReading: Kotomine tentatively contrasts Rin’s positive and Sakura’s negative disposition or polarity.
findings.explanation: The English reifies them as “the positive” and “the negative,” obscuring temperament or polarity and weakening the tentative claim.

findings.highlight: he contacted you
findings.evidenceJa: 臓硯がおまえに手を出してきた
findings.governingReading: Zouken made a move against or interfered with Shirou because Sakura exceeded his expectations.
findings.explanation: The English reduces hostile intervention to neutral contact.

findings.highlight: If she can survive the emergence, she should not die
findings.evidenceJa: 羽化に耐えられるのであらば、母胎とて死にはすまい
findings.governingReading: If Sakura can withstand the entity’s emergence, even the maternal vessel may avoid death.
findings.explanation: The English makes survival the condition for not dying, losing the distinction between enduring emergence and the body’s conditional survival.

findings.highlight: do not let Zouken have her
findings.evidenceJa: 臓硯にだけは手渡すな
findings.governingReading: Above all, Shirou must not hand Sakura over to Zouken.
findings.explanation: The English weakens the active transfer warning into generic possession.
